findings.summary: When the same captain's next sortie takes the ship over from a pass (which the planner now schedules at the pass instant via passStartMs), the summoner's plate is cut: a following pass ignores `carry` and shows nothing in flight, and a following parked sortie snaps it to 0 at its park. So in a run of summons (Meteor Pod, F1) every summon but the chain's last is never named, which breaks Decided's 'its plate rides with the ship for NOTE_MIN_MS' and R14.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/chart/fx/movers.ts:393 `if (this.passS > 0) return ride(h, this.passS);` (h<0 in flight gives 0, carry unused); :394-396, the carry ride holds only while h<0, then `Math.min(1, h / foldS, ...)` is 0 at h=0; src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts:341 passStartMs starts the next gather at the pass; castLabels.crew picks the latest window, and interpreter.crew() reads the new Sortie's crewOpen. A read-only scan of the app's story-time plans (vite-node over scripts/pacing-ledger planOf, every pod): `{ passes: 62, cut: 34 }`, all Meteor Pod, e.g. `facility.enter@0/1915 | facility.enter@715/1915 | facility.enter@1430/1915 ...`, all by one agent: 34 summons are taken over within CREW_FOLD_MS of their pass, before their plate has unfurled. In the unit test's own case (tests/unit/maneuvers.test.ts:1012), objective.underway's gather is 500 ms (pace.ts:443), shorter than the 520 ms unfurl, so the summon's plate is never whole.

findings.summary: The tests stop at the pursue's arguments and the phase arithmetic. Nothing exercises the Sortie's pass path (no stop at the spot), the `carry` hand-off to a following sortie, or the plate's ride in `crewOpen`, so the takeover defect above passes every unit test.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "passS\|handoff\|carry\|Sortie(" tests/unit/*.ts` matches only the pursue-args test in tests/unit/commands.test.ts:242-254 (holdS 0, waitS undefined, passS > 0). The '50 ms' check, commands.test.ts:897-902, compares gatherAt + durS*1000 with phaseAtMs(act), both taken from the same phase spans.

findings.summary: The new pacingBuilt test's comment says Meteor's summons 'still wait for each tender's launch', but the plan chains them 715 ms apart, each setting off at the previous one's pass.
findings.evidence: tests/unit/pacingBuilt.test.ts:162; the Meteor Pod plan's first summon beat: `facility.enter@0/1915 54fde7 | facility.enter@715/1915 54fde7 | facility.enter@1430/1915 54fde7 | ...` with no attachment.open between them

acceptance.2: met in letter: commands.test.ts checks holdS 0 / no waitS, and that the blip and the station's act land within 50 ms (also on the interpreter and under reduced motion); the mover's no-stop path itself isn't tested.

The only schedule golden is director.json; it moved (Pulsar dropping the light lever, tempo 1.1→2), which is plausible from the saving, but the packet isn't available to check that it names each change.

summary: The engine side is clean and consistent: rule phases, the pass in the planner (no turn, passStartMs, no nearWaits), docs 05/13/15 and the ledger all agree, and typecheck plus the unit and golden suites pass. The renderer's hand-off loses the summoner's plate whenever the next sortie takes over at the pass, which is the common case in F1's bulk-summon pod, so 'named from the blip for NOTE_MIN_MS' doesn't hold there, and no test covers the mover.
